title: SNS and EventBridge fan-out to SQS
hook: One domain event often needs multiple independent consumers. Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) and Amazon EventBridge fan a single publish to many Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) queues — each consumer scales and fails independently.

blocks.text: SNS topic subscribers include SQS queues — SNS wraps the payload in its envelope JSON. EventBridge rules match events on a bus and target SQS with optional input transformation and dead-letter configuration. SQS buffers each downstream pipeline from spikes in the publisher. Queue policies must allow the publishing service principal.

blocks.text: Fan-out decouples teams: analytics slowdown does not block inventory. Missing queue policy is the top deploy failure — SNS cannot deliver without sqs:SendMessage permission. EventBridge adds content-based filtering and schema registry; SNS is simpler for pure multicast.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: SNS for simple fan-out; EventBridge for routing rules and cross-account. Always set queue policy with source ARN condition.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — SNS topic with SQS subscription and policy
snippet.code:
Resources:
  OrderTopic:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Topic
  InventoryQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: inventory-updates
  InventoryQueuePolicy:
    Type: AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy
    Properties:
      Queues: [!Ref InventoryQueue]
      PolicyDocument:
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: sns.amazonaws.com }
            Action: sqs:SendMessage
            Resource: !GetAtt InventoryQueue.Arn
            Condition:
              ArnEquals:
                aws:SourceArn: !Ref OrderTopic
  InventorySub:
    Type: AWS::SNS::Subscription
    Properties:
      Protocol: sqs
      TopicArn: !Ref OrderTopic
      Endpoint: !GetAtt InventoryQueue.Arn
      RawMessageDelivery: true
snippet.explanation: Queue policy is mandatory. RawMessageDelivery skips SNS wrapper for simpler Lambda parsing.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — EventBridge rule targeting SQS
snippet.code:
OrderPlacedRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      EventBusName: company-orders
      EventPattern:
        source: [orders.api]
        detail-type: [OrderPlaced]
      Targets:
        - Arn: !GetAtt AnalyticsQueue.Arn
          Id: analytics
          DeadLetterConfig:
            Arn: !GetAtt RuleDLQ.Arn
snippet.explanation: Rule DLQ catches delivery failures to SQS — separate from consumer DLQ.

snippet.label: TypeScript — publish to EventBridge
snippet.explanation: Detail is a JSON string. Rules match on source and detail-type; content filters use detail field paths.

snippet.label: TypeScript — unwrap SNS envelope from SQS body
snippet.explanation: Without raw delivery, SNS nests payload in Message string inside SQS body — common parse bug.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Missing SQS queue policy — silent subscription failure. Parsing SQS body without unwrapping SNS Message. No DLQ on EventBridge rule target. Same queue subscribed twice causing duplicate processing without idempotency.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: CloudWatch NumberOfMessagesSent on topic versus each queue — mismatch means filter policy or delivery failure. EventBridge FailedInvocations metric on rule. Enable SNS delivery status logging to S3 for audit.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'just publish to SQS from API three times.' Strong answer: single publish to bus/topic, queue policy, independent consumers, idempotent handlers per queue.

interviewTakeaways: SNS and EventBridge fan one event to many SQS queues — each consumer scales independently.
Queue policy must allow sns.amazonaws.com or events.amazonaws.com with source ARN condition.
Raw message delivery or unwrap SNS Message field — parse bugs are common in Lambda.
60s: Fan-out via SNS or EventBridge to per-service SQS. Queue policy required. Idempotent each consumer.
Follow-up: EventBridge archive and replay versus SNS?
commonPitfalls: Missing queue policy — top SNS-to-SQS deploy failure.
Strong answer: QueuePolicy with ArnEquals aws:SourceArn on topic or rule.
Forgetting SNS envelope when raw delivery disabled.
No rule DLQ — delivery failures invisible until messages silently drop.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node EventEmitter.emit to multiple listeners is in-process fan-out — SNS/EventBridge add durability and cross-service boundaries like C# MediatR notifications with out-of-process handlers.
Publishing OrderPlaced to EventBridge replaces in-memory event bus when extracting microservices — same event shape, different transport.
